name: NexPilot – Content Freshness & Review Manager
author: NexGrowix

sections.description:
NexPilot helps you keep WordPress content fresh, organized, and ready for review.

As your website grows, older posts and pages can easily become outdated or forgotten. NexPilot gives you a structured content maintenance workflow inside WordPress to identify content that needs attention, prioritize reviews, manage a review queue, and plan future content updates.

Whether you manage a blog, business website, content-heavy publication, or multiple client websites, NexPilot makes ongoing content reviews easier to organize.

Keep Track of Content Freshness

See which content is fresh, approaching review, or needs attention.

NexPilot helps you understand the current state of your content library so you can focus on the posts and pages that matter most.

Find Outdated Content

Stop manually checking hundreds of posts to find content that may need updating.

Use content freshness information and configurable review settings to identify older content that deserves another look.

Manage a Content Review Queue

Add important posts to a dedicated review queue and create a clear workflow for your next content updates.

Instead of keeping review tasks in spreadsheets, notes, or separate tools, manage the process directly inside WordPress.

Schedule Future Content Reviews

Content maintenance should not end after one update.

Set review cycles and next-review dates so important content can be checked again at the right time.

Content Freshness Score

Use freshness scores and statuses to quickly understand which content may require attention and prioritize your editorial work.

Content Audit Workflow

Review your existing content library, identify content that needs attention, organize your review work, and export content audit information when needed.

Marketer Content Brief

Keep useful editorial information with your content, including details that help organize content strategy and future reviews.

Weekly Review Digest

Stay aware of content that requires attention with scheduled review summaries.

Flexible Content Maintenance

Configure your review workflow to better match the way you manage your WordPress content.

NexPilot is designed to turn content maintenance into a repeatable process rather than an occasional manual audit.

Why Use NexPilot?

  • Find content that may need updating
  • Track content freshness from one place
  • Build an organized review queue
  • Schedule future content reviews
  • Create a repeatable editorial workflow
  • Audit existing WordPress content
  • Export content audit information
  • Keep the workflow inside WordPress
  • No external API required

Who Is NexPilot For?

NexPilot is useful for:

  • Bloggers maintaining older articles
  • Content marketers managing growing content libraries
  • Editorial teams planning regular content reviews
  • SEO teams reviewing existing content
  • Agencies maintaining client websites
  • Business websites with large post libraries
  • Website owners who want an organized content maintenance process

Common Use Cases

NexPilot can help when you need to:

  • Find WordPress posts that have not been reviewed recently
  • Identify outdated content across a growing website
  • Build a monthly content review queue
  • Prioritize older articles for updating
  • Schedule the next review after updating a post
  • Perform a WordPress content audit
  • Export content information for reporting
  • Maintain an ongoing editorial review workflow

A Simple Content Review Workflow

NexPilot helps you follow a repeatable process:

  1. Review your content freshness dashboard.
  2. Identify content that needs attention.
  3. Prioritize important posts.
  4. Add content to the review queue.
  5. Review and update the content.
  6. Mark the content as reviewed.
  7. Schedule the next review when needed.

This helps turn content maintenance from a one-time task into an ongoing WordPress workflow.

Privacy Friendly

NexPilot does not require an external API or external dashboard for its core content review workflow.

Your editorial and review information stays within your WordPress website.

Privacy

NexPilot stores content review dates, editorial activity, review queue information, and optional marketing brief fields in the site’s own database. An assigned content owner is stored as a WordPress user ID. NexPilot does not contact external services, use telemetry, or share this information with NexGrowix.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin folder to /wp-content/plugins/ or install the ZIP from Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin.
  2. Activate NexPilot.
  3. Open NexPilot in the WordPress admin menu.
  4. Review Settings and choose the post types and freshness thresholds you want.
sections.faq:
What does NexPilot do?

NexPilot helps you track content freshness, identify content that may need attention, manage a review queue, and organize ongoing content reviews inside WordPress.

What is content freshness?

Content freshness helps you understand how recently content has been updated or reviewed. NexPilot uses review information and configurable settings to organize content by freshness status.

Can NexPilot help me find outdated WordPress posts?

Yes. NexPilot is designed to help identify content that may need attention so you can prioritize posts and pages for review.

What is the Review Queue?

The Review Queue gives you a dedicated place to organize content you plan to review or update.

Can I schedule future content reviews?

NexPilot supports an ongoing review workflow so content can be reviewed again based on your configured review process.

Can I use NexPilot for a WordPress content audit?

Yes. NexPilot can help you review your content library, identify content that requires attention, organize review work, and export audit information.

Does NexPilot require an external API?

No. NexPilot does not require an external API for its core content freshness and review workflow.

Where is my review information stored?

NexPilot keeps its editorial and review information within your WordPress website.

Who should use NexPilot?

NexPilot can be useful for bloggers, content marketers, SEO teams, editorial teams, agencies, business websites, and anyone managing a growing WordPress content library.
sections.changelog:
1.1.7

  • Fixed several minor issues.
  • Improved overall stability and reliability.

1.1.6

  • Reduced the height of all four dashboard summary cards.
  • Enlarged and repositioned summary icons with a single subtle background bubble.
  • Expanded Review Activity with queue and snooze metrics for better use of space.
  • Removed Documentation and Support URL settings and connected both buttons directly to NexGrowix.

1.1.5

  • Rebuilt dashboard summary cards with clearer badge, number, icon, and supporting-text hierarchy.
  • Balanced the three lower dashboard panels and removed excessive fixed empty space.
  • Refined spacing, typography, focus, hover, and responsive behavior throughout the admin UI.
  • Removed all remaining box shadows, including editor fields, toggles, and notifications.

1.1.4

  • Added soft semantic colors back to dashboard summary icons and status rings.
  • Added subtle pastel bubble artwork to the four summary card backgrounds.
  • Restored clear color coding for Review, Queue, and View row actions.
  • Harmonized Quick Action and Review Activity accents without adding shadows.

1.1.3

  • Refined the dashboard with a calmer, neutral color system and minimal shadows.
  • Removed the colored accent strips from the lower dashboard panels.
  • Replaced long status bars with four compact circular status indicators.
  • Simplified card, quick-action, table-action, focus, and hover states.
  • Added a visible Support button and configurable Support URL setting.
  • Added reduced-motion support for a more comfortable admin experience.

1.1.2

  • Redesigned the post editor Content Brief into clear strategy and review sections.
  • Prevented the Content Brief from causing horizontal editor-sidebar overflow.
  • Disabled repeated review actions while content is Fresh.
  • Disabled duplicate queue actions while content is already pending or snoozed.
  • Restored queue availability automatically after a queued item is marked reviewed.
  • Added server-side state checks to protect action rules beyond the dashboard interface.

1.1.1

  • Improved dashboard and Settings typography for better readability.
  • Added a configurable Documentation button to the dashboard header.
  • Updated the WordPress admin menu icon.
  • Redesigned status, review activity, quick action, and table action controls.

1.1.0

  • Fixed the freshness score incorrectly showing 100% when all content was in Review Soon or when no content was tracked.
  • Added weighted and configurable freshness scoring.
  • Added NexGrowix branding inside NexPilot admin pages.
  • Added marketer Content Brief fields and dashboard filters.
  • Added custom review cycles and next review dates.
  • Added content audit CSV export.
  • Added email opt-in and privacy policy guidance.
  • Added dashboard display and marketing workflow settings.

1.0.0

  • Initial release.
